PositionSchedule.Name: This is a Regular Full-Time position with a minimum workweek of 40 hours and eligible for benefits.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Resumes must be two pages (or less). Resumes should clearly demonstrate the applicant's relevant experience, skills, knowledge and abilities as they pertain to this position. A qualified candidate must possess the following: Managerial or supervisory work experience of the caliber described above that demonstrates comprehensive analytical skills and acquired formal training in financial analysis and financial management systems. The work experience must be equivalent in difficulty and complexity to the next lower grade level. Must possess good oral communication and writing skills. Strong organizational skills are required. Must be able to manage multiple concurrent projects effectively and present ideas and proposals to a variety of audiences. Knowledge of standard office software such as word processing, graphics presentation, spreadsheet and e-mail. Preferred are those candidates that process 4 years experience in MWR operations and / or financial management programs that provided a general knowledge of overall MWR operations and operational experience in hospitality operations, financial analysis, and budget operations. A Graduate degree in finance, accounting, or business is also preferred, however; adequate training and experience can be an acceptable substitute. In addition to the above qualifications, candidates who possess the following qualifications will be considered "Highly Preferred" or "Best Qualified": Possess at least 3 years of leadership experience in MWR Business Operations with demonstrated success in financial management, operational performance, and human capital management. Possess experience overseeing operations such as bowling, golf, food and beverage, bingo, or other Category B and C Community Recreation programs. Possess applicable training or certifications related to MWR Business Operations. Possess experience managing multiple programs simultaneously within a large, complex MWR organization. In order to be considered for the highly preferred criteria, your resume must show that you meet BOTH the minimum qualifications, and ALL of the high preferred criteria. Applicants meeting ALL criteria will be considered best qualified, and will be referred to the selecting official first. Remaining applicants will be referred for consideration if the certificate (referral list) is returned with no selection.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located at ID-Western Hemisphere Command, Fort Bragg, NC. PCS Costs and Incentives Permanent Change of Station (PCS) costs may be authorized. Incentives will not be paid. Army NAF paysetting rules apply to this vacancy.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Fort Bragg, recognized with the 2025 Exemplary Workforce Development Award, is an ideal place for MWR professionals to grow and succeed. Located in the heart of North Carolina, it boasts a culturally diverse setting, blending rural charm with urban amenities. Residents benefit from a temperate year-round climate, proximity to world-renowned colleges, and easy access to both beaches (2 hours) and mountains (3 hours) via I-95. The community offers a wealth of facilities and services, including first-class golfing, a professional skeet range, an ice skating rink, quality childcare, pet daycare, and a vibrant calendar of community events.
MajorDuties: Serves as a senior program analyst for Business and Recreation Programs at the ID-WH Region FMWR Office providing subject matter expertise and recommendations to region and garrison leadership at echelon on FMWR business program performance.

Evaluates overall MWR NAF revenue-producing operations to identify problems and recommend effective and economical ways to solve problems, meet needs, and produce efficiencies. Recommends and develops future MWR programs and activities.

Analyzes policy issues and develops programs, policies, procedures and practices that promote economy, efficiency and effectiveness in MWR operations. Monitors implementation and compliance with established policies and programs.
Acts as a technical expert in a professional field; uses in-depth specialized knowledge and experience to develop new approaches to issues previously unresponsive to accepted methods.

Develops in-depth analysis and evaluates trends of garrison performance to support local requirements. Interprets on own initiative; completed work reviewed for feasibility, effectiveness and compatibility with other work.

We offer a wide range of career opportunities, including jobs in childcare, recreation, hospitality, and more. NAF flexible employees, working in the United States or a U.S. citizen or spouse or child of a U.S. citizen working for a NAFI in a foreign area, are eligible to participate in the NAF 401(k) plan. Details.JobSummary: Store Associates work either independently or as part of a team in any assigned retail area of a commissary store within the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) system, performing a variety of duties including handling, preparing, and stocking grocery and produce items, and checking-out customer purchases. Specific assignments vary by individual store and store management requirements.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: As an international grocery chain, the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) operates 235 commissaries throughout the world, with annual sales of more than $4 billion. We are proud to support military family readiness and enhance quality of life for our military service members and their families through this valued benefit. The foundation for our mission success is our people. We are more than 13,000 strong and reflect our nation's diverse cultures and backgrounds. We are a grocery store and a whole lot more. More information.
MajorDuties: Assisting customers by answering questions such as item price or location, and handling bulky/heavy items. Operating an electronic checkout system to record unit price, total customer purchase, and make change. Performing a variety of duties in handling, preparing and maintaining stock levels of grocery and produce items. Reviewing stock levels and gathering inventory data in order to maintain the Computer Assisted Ordering (CAO) system. Preparing and maintaining a variety of documents to order commissary items, reconcile invoices and submit requisitions. Maintaining security, safety, and sanitation practices and procedures. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: **Announcement closing date has been extended to 7/31/2026** Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. Current Civilian Employees of the Defense Health Agency (DHA) Current Term Defense Health Agency HQs Research and Development Employee Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Reserve (MR) and National Guard (NG) Technician Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD MR and NG Preference Eligible Tech Receiving Disability Retirement Priority Placement Program, DoD Retained Grade Preference Eligible DHA Research & Development (R&D) is participating in an alternative personnel system known as the Personnel Demonstration Project (PDP). The DJ-03 payband is equivalent to the GS-11 step 1 to GS-12 step 10 level. In keeping with the Demonstration pay fixing policies, employees earning a salary that falls within this payband equivalent, may not receive an immediate pay increase (promotion) if appointed to this position. Future pay increases within the payband will be accomplished through the pay for performance management system. In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1. Experience administering a travel management system such as the Defense Travel System (i.e. managing traveler profiles, creating routing lists, preparing travel orders and/or travel vouchers) 2. Experience monitoring a budget that includes the identification, selection, and/or approval for information technology and information management (IT/IM) equipment purchases 3. Experience performing contract officer representative duties including using Management Information Systems (MIS) such as Virtual Contracting Enterprise Paperless Contract File (VCE-PCF), Wide Area Workflow (WAWF) and General Fund Enterprise Business System (GFEBS) 4. Experience utilizing a credit card to procure equipment, supplies, training, and/or contracts This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (DJ-02/GS-09). OR Education: Ph.D or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M. in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: General Studies, Business, or Management (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Attention to Detail Customer Service Decision Making Flexibility Integrity/Honesty Interpersonal Skills Learning Reading Comprehension Reasoning Self-Management Stress Tolerance Teamwork

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: MRDC is now part of the Defense Health Agency (DHA) Research & Development (R&D). We are the medical materiel developer, with responsibility for medical research, development and acquisition. Our expertise in these critical areas helps establish and maintain the capabilities the military needs to remain ready and lethal on the battlefield. Please visit our website https://mrdc.health.mil/ **Announcement closing date has been extended to 7/31/2026**
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: As an integrated health care system, the Defense Health Agency delivers healthcare services across the Department of Defense and enables combat support to the Joint Force as a strategic partner. Through a robust healthcare delivery system, and a dedicated team of inspired professionals, the Agency ensures the worldwide delivery of medical, dental, and pharmacy programs to more than 9.5 million uniformed service members, retirees, and their families, by improving health and building readiness Anytime, Anywhere-Always.
MajorDuties: Receive and process information management and information technology (IM/IT) purchase requests from DHA Research and Development offices
Perform duties of Contracting Officer Representative
Ensure payments are made to vendors using Wide Area Workflow
Process purchase requests using the General Fund Enterprise Business System
Primary Credit Card holder for DHA Research and Development IM/IT purchases
Develop Statements of Work and Performance Work Statements
Collaboration with multiple offices and staff to complete purchases process
Prepare a variety of correspondence, letters, reports, and briefings
Review correspondence for formatting, grammar, and spelling errors
As Records Manager, is responsible for the proper retention and disposition of files
Prepare, coordinate and schedule, CONUS and OCONUS travel authorizations and vouchers within the Defense Travel System (DTS)

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The city of Frederick lies in Frederick County, Maryland, where hip meets historic every day. Here, scenic landscapes provide thrill-seekers with adventure, and cutting-edge cuisine is served up in Civil War-era buildings alongside unique specialty shops, galleries, museums and theaters. Located less than one hour from Washington, D.C., Baltimore, and Gettysburg, the city of Frederick, Maryland is surrounded by mountain views, wineries, orchards and vibrant Main Street communities. Visitors can hike on the Appalachian Trail, visit Maryland's largest brewery, and tour a battlefield all in one day.The Installation Management Command (IMCOM) G-9 mission is to create and maintain "FIRST CHOICE" Family and Morale, Welfare & Recreation (FMWR) programs and services for America's Army, essential to a ready, self-reliant force.
MajorDuties: Through subordinate activity managers, is responsible for the overall management and direction of the Directorate, Morale Welfare and Recreation (DMWR) Support Division at a small/medium garrison.

To include some of the following activities: NAF Financial Management, Marketing, NAF Major Construction (Requirements Determination), Private Organization, Commercial Sponsorship, NAF Property Management, Internal Review/Management Controls etc.

Reviews and evaluates progress of program plans to determine whether overall objectives are being accomplished economically with reference to budget and manpower.

Serves on a variety of activity councils to keep informed of operations and/or to coordinate programs and requirements. Serves as the garrison focal point for DMWR Support Management policies and practices. Performs other duties as assigned.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located at The Peak & Pine Plains Bowling Center. Join our team at the Directorate of Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation (FMWR) at Fort Drum. We are dedicated to enhancing the lives of Soldiers and their Families by providing essential support services, including child and youth programs and a variety of recreational activities that directly contribute to Soldier readiness and well-being. Incentives and Bonuses Incentives will NOT be paid.
Details.SubAgencyName: Directorate of Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Fort Drum, home of the 10th Mountain Division (LI), is in northern New York's picturesque North Country, one of the most historically unique and geographically beautiful areas of the United States offering many outdoor recreational opportunities from hunting and fishing to winter sports. Fort Drum is approximately 30 miles south of the Canadian border, 85 miles north of Syracuse, and 350 miles north of New York City. Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation (FMWR) employees enjoy great benefits and unique opportunities including competitive salaries; flexible, part time/full time positions; career diversity and progression; paid leave; medical, dental, vision, life insurance, flexible spending account options and 401K/retirement. FMWR employees are provided job-related training and continued educational opportunities; have access to use free state of the art fitness facilities and a pool; opportunities to work special events to include festivals, 5k runs, and recreational activities while serving our military community; can enjoy Hyper Bowl entertainment, recreational lodging, discounted tickets for theme and local attractions; rent boats, campers, party equipment, etc.; and receive discounted child care while employed by Child and Youth Services (CYS). A career with FMWR awaits you and is your gateway to travel and work at any one of more than 70 U.S. Army installations worldwide. We are excited to welcome you to Team Drum!
MajorDuties: Provides hands-on supervision of all restaurant operations, occasionally assisting with serving, hosting, or cooking to set the pace and ensure a smooth workflow during peak hours.
Enforces operational standards by ensuring staff follow established schedules, recipes, and procedures, while also monitoring guest flow and service ticket times to maintain consistency.
Manages the guest experience by providing information, conducting table visits to ensure satisfaction, and maintaining order, seeking assistance from military police when necessary.
Handles administrative and financial duties, including overseeing cash and inventory, supervising employee timekeeping and performance reporting, and performing opening/closing security checks.

Details.Benefits: Working for Army Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF) can offer numerous advantages. Army NAF employment can provide a sense of pride and fulfillment, as you'll be supporting communities comprised of military and civilian personnel, and their families, which contributes to the Department of Defense's overall mission. We offer a wide range of career opportunities, including jobs in childcare, recreation, hospitality, and more. Many employees have opportunities for professional development, including training, education, and certification programs to help towards career advancement. As an Army NAF employee, you'll have access to some on-base facilities, including fitness centers, libraries, and many other amenities. Regular full-time and part-time employees are eligible for enrollment in health and life insurance, participation in 401k and retirement plans, and paid personal time off and federal holidays. NAF flexible employees, working in the United States or a U.S. citizen or spouse or child of a U.S. citizen working for a NAFI in a foreign area, are eligible to participate in the NAF 401(k) plan. Some flexible employees may also be eligible to receive health insurance. For a slideshow presentation regarding these benefits, please click the Review Our Benefits link below.
Details.OtherInformation: This is a Standing Register job announcement creating a pool of qualified applicants. Candidates will be referred to hiring officials as positions become available. The first consideration period for applications ended on 1/6/2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST. Applications received after this date will only be considered if more vacancies arise. Area of Consideration This job is open to U.S. Citizens and Non-U.S. Nationals who meet these requirements: You must live within 100 miles of Fort Drum, NY., AND If you are a Non-U.S. National, you must have lived in the U.S. or a U.S. Territory for at least three years in a row right before starting this job. Spouse Employment Preference (SEP) and Involuntarily Separated Military Preference (ISMP) are included in this area of consideration. Manual Application Option If you are unable to apply online, you can complete a paper application. To get started, contact servicing NAF Human Resources representative or office listed in the Agency Contact Information section (at the bottom of this announcement) to request a copy of the application form. Be sure to submit your completed application form, along with your resume and any required supporting documents, no later than 3:00 p.m. EST by Initial Cut-Off date to receive first consideration but no later than 3:00 p.m. EST on 09/30/2026 to ensure timely processing. Important: Incomplete applications, including missing responses to questionnaire items may result in an ineligible rating. PCS Costs Payment of Permanent Change of Station (PCS) costs are NOT authorized based on a determination that a PCS move is NOT in the Government's interest. Allowances and Differentials This job is part of a pay-banded system. Sunday Premium and Night Differential pay have NOT been authorized by the Garrison Commander or the Collective Bargaining Agreement for Flexible positions with no guaranteed hours. Non-foreign overseas allowances, cost of living (COLA), and differentials will NOT be paid. Important Information Regarding Access to Certain Federal Facilities: Access to certain federal facilities may require a REAL ID-compliant driver's license/ID (marked with a star) or an Enhanced Driver's License (EDL) from WA, MI, MN, NY, or VT. See https://www.tsa.gov/real-id for details. Your Application may be Considered for Multiple Opportunities: After you apply, your application remains valid for 90 days and may be referred to hiring officials as new vacancies arise. Additional referrals may occur for up to 90 days after the closing date. Termination of Spouse Employment Preference Refusal of a military spouse to participate in established recruitment procedures for a Regular Full-Time (RFT) or Regular Part-Time (RPT) position (for example, interview, and so forth) is considered a declination of employment and is a basis for termination of Spouse Employment Preference (SEP) entitlement for the current Permanent Change of Station (PCS) of the sponsor. Discover Your Path to Success Before you apply, take a moment to explore our Applicant Information Kit, your go-to guide for understanding our hiring processes and making your application stand out. Inside you will find helpful tips, insights, and everything you need to feel confident and prepared. Click this URL to view the kit: https://publicfileshare.chra.army.mil/Applicants/NAF_Applicant_Information_Kit.pdf.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: CYBER EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITIONS ARE NOT SUBJECT TO THE TWO-PAGE RESUME LIMIT. YOUR FULL RESUME WILL NEED TO BE UPLOADED TO YOUR USAJOBS PROFILE USING THE DOCUMENT TYPE "OTHER DOCUMENTS". This position is in the Professional work category at the Full Performance work level within the CES Occupational Structure. Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Army CES positions apply Veteran's Preference to preference eligible candidates, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 3005, "CES Employment and Placement". If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe one-year specialized experience that demonstrates the possession of knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Such experience is typically in or directly related to the work of the position to be filled. Specialized experience would be demonstrated by: Conducting operational and tactical level planning in support of cyberspace operations. Assisting in the development of contingency and crisis plans, such as Operations Orders (OPORDs), Operations Plans (OPLANs), Warning Orders (WARNOs), and Fragmentary Orders (FRAGOs). Collecting and analyzing information related to cyberspace operations, signal intelligence, and electronic warfare to identify intelligence gaps and advise on findings.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is a DOD Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system position in the Excepted Service under 10 USC 1599f. Employees occupying CES positions are in the Excepted Service and must adhere to U.S. Code, Title 10, as well as Department of Defense Instruction 1400.25. This position is located at Fort Gordon, Georgia.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Serves as a Cyber Planner in Joint Force Headquarters-Cyber (JFHQ-C), Army Cyber Command (ARCYBER).
Participates in the development of Operations Orders (OPORDs), Operations Plans (OPLANs), Warning Orders (WARNOs), and Fragmentary Orders (FRAGOs) supporting Combatant Command (CCMD) Warfighters
Integrates and synchronizes cyberspace operations effects with the Joint Warfighter’s plan of action.
Develops and maintains contingency and crisis action plans to support the full range of cyberspace operations.
Employs the Army Operations Process, the Joint Operations and Execution System (JOPES), and the Integrated Joint Special Technical Operations (IJSTO) system.
Participates in targeting selection, validation, synchronization, and execution of complex cyber missions.
Collaborates with cyber operators to identify and levy requirements for information, collection, analysis, and effects.
Collaborates with cyber operators, analysts, and Research, Development, Testing, and Evaluation staff members to gain access and technical information to meet planning objectives.
Details.Education: Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted.
Details.Evaluations: Once the announcement has closed, a review of your application package (resume, supporting documents, and responses to the questionnaire) will be used to determine whether you meet the qualification requirements listed on this announcement. If, after reviewing your resume and/or supporting documentation, a determination is made that you have inflated your qualifications and/or experience, you may lose consideration for this position.

Details.RequiredDocuments: WARNING: DO NOT INCLUDE CLASSIFIED INFORMATION IN YOUR APPLICATION PACKET! Application packages that contain Classified information WILL NOT receive consideration for this position. Should you submit a resume or any other document as part of your application package and it is confirmed that any of the information is Classified, in addition to being found ineligible for consideration for this position, your Security Office will be notified to determine if any further action is warranted. The documents you are required to submit vary based on the authority you are using to apply (i.e., applying as a veteran, applying as a current permanent Federal employee, applying as a reinstatement, etc). Please review the following links to see which documents you need to provide to prove your eligibility to apply: Applicant Checklist for Internal/Merit Promotion Announcements. As described above, your complete application includes your resume, your responses to the online questionnaire, and documents which prove your eligibility to apply. If you fail to provide these documents, you will be marked as having an incomplete application package and you will not be considered any further. 1. Your resume: Cyber Excepted Service positions are not subject to the two-page resume limit. Your full resume will need to be uploaded to your USAJOBS profile using the document type 'Other Documents'. Your resume may be submitted in any format and must support the specialized experience described in this announcement. For each relevant work experience, make sure you include the employer's name, job title, start and end dates (include month and year), for qualifications purposes, the number of hours worked per week, and a brief description that show you can perform the tasks at the required level listed in the job announcement. If your resume does not contain this information, your application may be marked as incomplete, and you may not receive consideration for this position. Use plain language. Avoid using acronyms and terms that are not easily understood. The hiring agency will not make assumptions about what's in your resume. If your resume includes a photograph or other inappropriate material or content, it will not be used to make eligibility and qualification determinations, and you may not be considered for this vacancy. For additional information, to include formatting tips, see: What to include in your resume. 2. Other supporting documents: Cover Letter, optional Most recent Performance Appraisal, if applicable Proof of Eligibility to Apply: Your application must include the documents which prove you are eligible to apply for the vacancy. The Proof of Eligibility document describes authorities commonly used in merit promotion recruitment and what document(s) are required to prove you meet the requirements of the authority. You must meet the requirements of at least one of the authorities listed in the Who May Apply section above to receive further consideration. NOTE: Documents submitted as part of the application package, to include supplemental documents, may be shared beyond the Human Resources Office. Some supplemental documents such as military orders and marriage certificates may contain personal information for someone other than you. You may sanitize these documents to remove another person's personal information before you submit your application. You may be asked to provide an un-sanitized version of the documents if you are selected to confirm your eligibility.
Details.OtherInformation: If you are a current federal career/career-conditional employee, you will be placed on an excepted appointment. Male applicants born after December 31, 1959, must complete a Pre-Employment Certification Statement for Selective Service Registration. You will be required to provide proof of U.S. Citizenship. This position requires a 3 year probationary period during which the agency evaluates your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In making this determination, the agency may consider your performance and conduct; agency needs and interests; whether your continued employment supports organizational or Government goals; and whether it promotes the efficiency of the Federal service. Continued employment requires written certification that it advances the public interest. Direct Deposit of Pay is required. Must be able to obtain and maintain a Top Secret/SCI security clearance. Selection is subject to restrictions resulting from Department of Defense referral system for displaced employees. If you have retired from federal service and you are interested in employment as a reemployed annuitant, see the information in the Reemployed Annuitant information sheet. This is a(n) 71 Career Field position. Multiple positions may be filled from this announcement. Salary includes applicable locality pay or Local Market Supplement. When you perform a Civilian Permanent Change of Station (PCS) with the government, the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) considers the majority of your entitlements to be taxable. Visit https://www.dfas.mil/civilianemployees/civrelo/Civilian-Moving-Expenses-Tax-Deduction/ for more information. Permanent Change of Station (PCS) allowances may be authorized, subject to the provisions of the Joint Travel Regulations and an agency determination that a PCS move is in the Government Interest. Recruitment and Relocation incentives MAY be authorized for highly qualified candidates. Advanced In-Hire incentive MAY be authorized for highly qualified candidates. Advanced Leave Accrual incentive MAY be authorized for highly qualified candidates. This position has a DCWF Primary work role code of 332.

They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Serves as USCYBERCOM and JCPG Weapons and Tactics Director (WTD), leads a cohort of Cyber Mission Force (CMF) personnel and can perform the duties that exploit computer components and architectures.
Leads and manages exceptionally technical personnel to include interactive operators, exploitation analysts, mission commanders, capability developers, and other technical directors.

Incorporates computer network operators, network analysts, capability developers and technical leads from multiple organizations to optimize analysis, evaluation, planning, development, preparation and execution of JFHQ-C operations

YOUR FULL RESUME WILL NEED TO BE UPLOADED TO YOUR USAJOBS PROFILE USING THE DOCUMENT TYPE "OTHER DOCUMENTS". This position is in the Professional work category at the Full Performance work level within the CES Occupational Structure. Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Army CES positions apply Veteran's Preference to preference eligible candidates, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 3005, "CES Employment and Placement". If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe one year of specialized experience that demonstrates the possession of knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Such experience is typically in or directly related to the work of the position to be filled. Specialized experience would be demonstrated by providing technical expertise and guidance to decision makers in regard to planning and synchronizing offensive cyberspace operations; conducting offensive cyberspace operations planning to address the information environment and and contingency response operations; participates in planning and group events with the goal of proper development and publication of targeting guidance for military objectives and assigned missions; trains, instructs and maintains staff on various fires, targeting topics and other necessary training requirements for cyberspace operations

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is a DOD Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system position in the Excepted Service under 10 USC 1599f. Employees occupying CES positions are in the Excepted Service and must adhere to U.S. Code, Title 10, as well as Department of Defense Instruction 1400.25. This position is located at Fort Gordon, GA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Provides technical expertise and guidance to commanders and decision makers with respect to targeting effects and possible collateral effects to better inform decisions.

Planning efforts will focus primarily on nation states, non-state actors, criminal and terrorist organizations, and other threat actor operations within the Command’s global area of responsibility (AOR) with respect to targeting efforts.
Participates in combatant command (CCMD) boards, bureaus, cells, centers, and working groups in the conduct of planning for crisis and contingency operations

Trains and instructs staff from a variety of commands/organizations on relevant fires and targeting topics including, but not limited to: CEE, weaponeering, effects assessments, and the joint targeting cycle.

Will serve as a joint targeting, fire support, and collateral effects estimation (CEE) subject-matter expert for Army Cyber (ARCYBER) OCO operational planning teams (OPTs), and other joint and interagency working groups, as directed.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Researches, evaluates, analyzes, advises, and implements innovative solutions that increase quality and efficiency of operations conducted across ARCYBER JFHQ-C.
Serves as a command exploitation analyst (EA) that carries out network reconnaissance and vulnerability analyses and planning efforts
The incumbent leads and manages exceptionally technical personnel to include EAs, mission commanders, capability developers, and other technical advisors.

Reviews, ensures quality control, continuity of testing, documentation, distribution of guidance and approving tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) when delegated by USCYBERCOM and JCPG as part of mission management.

The incumbent assists with integrating CO capabilities into operations, exercise, design, integration, and synchronization of cyber related effects.

Presents information both written and orally on computer network topology and telecommunications architecture, their components, concepts, associated protocols, and theories of network communications.

Through regular review of message traffic, intelligence information, data analysis, and from other sources of information, identifies intelligence gaps, then assists in the development of operational programs to meet the identified need.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located at: Outdoor Recreation - Fort Hood, Texas. Outdoor Recreation at Fort Hood offers high-energy, customer-focused outdoor adventures including paintball, boating, hiking, camping, fishing, and family-friendly events. The team supports Soldiers and families with safe, fun, hands-on activities that build morale, resilience, and community connection.
Details.SubAgencyName: Family and Morale, Welfare & Recreation (FMWR) - Outdoor Recreation
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Fort Hood "A Great Place" rests in the beautiful 'hill and lake' country of Central Texas between Killeen and Copperas Cove and is approximately 60 miles north of the capital city of Austin, 50 miles south of Waco, 160 miles south of Dallas, and 150 miles north of San Antonio. For everyone who enjoys the outdoors, The Great Place is the ideal location, because of warm winters and hot summers. The nearby lakes, Belton and Stillhouse, offer year-round outdoor recreation activities.
MajorDuties: Independently performs customer service relations work that contributes toward the well-being of both civilian and military guests and the protection and safety of these guests, other employees and government property.
Uses tact and diplomacy to deny entrance to unauthorized personnel or to remove those not adhering to rules and policies, including those whose dress or manner does not meet prescribed standards.
Checks membership cards of persons entering the facility. Ensures that patrons comply with applicable rules and standards. Reports incidents to proper authorities.

Maintains assigned area in a clean and orderly manner. Ensures compliance with fire, safety and security standards. Maintains log of authorized visitors and checks to ensure visitors are authorized entry. May operate a motor vehicle.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes Analyzing program operational data using established analytical methods to identify inefficiencies and support workflow improvements; Preparing routine resource and administrative reports by reconciling financial data to ensure accurate tracking of divisional allocations; Processing routine personnel actions in accordance with agency regulations to resolve staff inquiries and maintain administrative compliance. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Business Administration or Business Management. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-07).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Management Analyst providing comprehensive analysis as a consultant to improve mission effectiveness, resource efficiency and Human Resources administrative support to the Directorate of Public Works, Business Operations, Human Resources Branch.
Details.SubAgencyName: Fort Hood, Directorate of Public Works, Business Operations
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Performs analytical work involved with various programs to include gathering data, analyzing information and recommending alternative courses of action, planning and tracking data gathered.
Organizes and documents findings of studies and prepares recommendations for implementation.
Performs and coordinates specific management and statistical studies which are initiated by the Division Chief.
Reviews feeder reports for completeness, accuracy, and conformity with prescribed criteria for reporting.
Prepare reports for submission to higher headquarters.
Develops, evaluates, and recommends improvements to management policies, practices, organizations functions, operating procedures, manpower utilization, controls, and structure.
Normally works on portions of a broader assignment carried out by a senior analyst.
Determines need for and conduct basic fact-finding applicable to the function or process studied.
Reviews precedents, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and information provided by the Director, Division Chief or HR Branch Chief.
Assist Director, Branch and Division Chiefs to resolve problems, plan implementation or testing of recommended changes, and follow up to evaluate effectiveness of improvements made.
Serves as liaison or activity's civilian personnel coordinator to assist managers and employees with civilian personnel processes.
Coordinates personnel actions with Director, Branch and Division Chiefs on status of personnel resources.
Analyzes budget, accounting and operating information in the development and preparation of budget data, worksheets, and reports.

See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. 30 Percent or More Disabled Veterans Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Current Department of Defense (DOD) Civilian Employee (non-Army) Domestic Defense Industrial Base/Major Range and Test Facilities Base Civilian Personnel Workforce Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Non-Appropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) Non-Department of Defense (DoD) Transfer People with Disabilities, Schedule A Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Reserve (MR) and National Guard (NG) Technician Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD MR and NG Preference Eligible Tech Receiving Disability Retirement Priority Placement Program, DoD Retained Grade Preference Eligible Reinstatement Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 Veterans Recruitment Appointment (VRA) In order to qualify, you must meet the experience or education requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: Have one year of specialized experience which includes the following. 1) provide research and information to analyze difficult and complex problems reported by computer users for issues such as specific software applications or operating systems; 2) Assist the director in managing the organization's computer processes or resources; and 3) visit job sites to collect data such as engineering specifications pertaining to various facilities or associate utility systems. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-09) OR Have successfully completed a Ph.D or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the work of the position, such as Major study-computer science, information science, information systems management, mathematics, statistics, operations research, or engineering, or course work that required the development or adaptation of computer programs and systems and provided knowledge equivalent to a major in the computer field. (NOTE: You must attach a copy of your transcripts for verification). OR Have specialized experience as described in A, but less than one year; and I have at least two years of graduate education as described in B, but less than the required three years. I have computed the percentage of the requirements that I meet, and the total is at least 100% (To compute the percentage, divide your total months of qualifying experience by 12. Then, divide your semester hours of graduate education beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. The total percentage must equal at least 100 percent to qualify.). (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) You will be evaluated on the basis of your level of competency in the following areas: Attention to Detail Customer Service Decision Making Flexibility Integrity/Honesty Interpersonal Skills Learning Reading Comprehension Reasoning Self-Management Stress Tolerance Teamwork Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-9).

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Fort Lee, Home of Logistic Warriors, is a US Army installation located near the Tri-Cities of Petersburg, Colonial Heights, and Hopewell, VA. Fort Lee is south of Richmond, the Capital of Virginia. There are several important missions accomplished by the activities located here. The missions accomplished at Fort Lee include combat and training development and the professional development of military personnel through various training programs. The civilian employees serve a vital role in direct support of the US Army mission that is crucial to supporting military operations. Fort Lee offers a broad range of civilian employment opportunities for people. The FMWR mission is to create and maintain "FIRST CHOICE" MWR products and services for America's Army, essential to a ready, self-reliant force. The Family and Morale Welfare and Recreation (FMWR) wants you to join our team! The FMWR is known for delivering optimum service to the community. We encourage you to join our team where you will truly make a difference in the lives of our American Soldiers and their families.

Details.Benefits: Working for Army Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF) can offer numerous advantages. Army NAF employment can provide a sense of pride and fulfillment, as you'll be supporting communities comprised of military and civilian personnel, and their families, which contributes to the Department of Defense's overall mission. We offer a wide range of career opportunities, including jobs in childcare, recreation, hospitality, and more. Many employees have opportunities for professional development, including training, education, and certification programs to help towards career advancement. As an Army NAF employee, you'll have access to some on-base facilities, including fitness centers, libraries, and many other amenities. Regular full-time and part-time employees are eligible for enrollment in health and life insurance, participation in 401k and retirement plans, and paid personal time off and federal holidays. NAF flexible employees, working in the United States or a U.S. citizen or spouse or child of a U.S. citizen working for a NAFI in a foreign area, are eligible to participate in the NAF 401(k) plan. Some flexible employees may also be eligible to receive health insurance. For a slideshow presentation regarding these benefits, please click the link below.

Details.SubAgencyName: Fort Lee, VA - NAF - MWR - Business Recreation Divison
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Fort Lee, Home of Logistic Warriors, is a US Army installation located near the Tri-Cities of Petersburg, Colonial Heights, and Hopewell, VA. Fort Lee is south of Richmond, the Capital of Virginia. There are several important missions accomplished by the activities located here. The missions accomplished at Fort Lee include combat and training development and the professional development of military personnel through various training programs. The civilian employees serve a vital role in direct support of the US Army mission that is crucial to supporting military operations. Fort Lee offers a broad range of civilian employment opportunities for people. The FMWR mission is to create and maintain "FIRST CHOICE" MWR products and services for America's Army, essential to a ready, self-reliant force. The Family and Morale Welfare and Recreation (FMWR) wants you to join our team! The FMWR is known for delivering optimum service to the community. We encourage you to join our team where you will truly make a difference in the lives of our American Soldiers and their families.
MajorDuties: Monitors operations to ensure smooth running of the business operation during evening hours and adherence to established schedules of activities and priorities. Assures the presence of personnel to carry out the services offered.

Provides information concerning services, prices, dress codes, standards of behavior, and special events. Opens and closes the facility and performs fire and security checks. Keeps an operational log while on duty.

Maintains order and harmony. As necessary, seeks assistance from military police, to control unacceptable behavior. Assumes responsibility for cash during tour of duty "cash collected" checks, check cashing.
Provides administrative supervision to employees. Checks employees in and out. Reports to functional supervisors on employee performance.
Conducts inventory at beginning and end of tour. Performs other duties as assigned.

Details.Benefits: Working for Army Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF) can offer numerous advantages. Army NAF employment can provide a sense of pride and fulfillment, as you'll be supporting communities comprised of military and civilian personnel, and their families, which contributes to the Department of Defense's overall mission. We offer a wide range of career opportunities, including jobs in childcare, recreation, hospitality, and more. Many employees have opportunities for professional development, including training, education, and certification programs to help towards career advancement. As an Army NAF employee, you'll have access to some on-base facilities, including fitness centers, libraries, and many other amenities. Regular full-time and part-time employees are eligible for enrollment in health and life insurance, participation in 401k and retirement plans, and paid personal time off and federal holidays. NAF flexible employees, working in the United States or a U.S. citizen or spouse or child of a U.S. citizen working for a NAFI in a foreign area, are eligible to participate in the NAF 401(k) plan. Some flexible employees may also be eligible to receive health insurance. For a slideshow presentation regarding these benefits, please click the link below.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Store Operations Group, Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA). The primary purpose of this position is to provide the manager with objectively based information for making decisions on the administrative and programmatic aspects of DeCA Store Operations and management.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: As an international grocery chain, the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) operates 235 commissaries throughout the world, with annual sales of more than $4 billion. We are proud to support military family readiness and enhance quality of life for our military service members and their families through this valued benefit. The foundation for our mission success is our people. We are more than 13,000 strong and reflect our nation's diverse cultures and backgrounds. We are a grocery store and a whole lot more. More information. Our Vision To be THE grocery provider of choice for our eligible patrons - delivering a vital benefit exclusively for our military community and their families. Our Mission Deliver a vital benefit of the military pay system that provides grocery items at significant savings while enhancing quality of life and readiness. DeCA HQ at Fort Lee VA is approximately 30 miles south of Richmond - a city of culture, cuisine, art, and outdoor activities - and situated alongside Petersburg, Colonial Heights, and Hopewell (the Tri-Cities of Virginia) and the neighboring counties of Chesterfield, Dinwiddie, and Prince George. We are approximately 90 miles from Tidewater, VA and about 130 miles from Washington D.C.
MajorDuties: As an Operations Coordinator, you will be responsible for the following duties: Provides the manager and senior leadership with analysis, studies, and objectively based information to support decisions on Store Operations programs. Serves as Portfolio Manager by managing performance data, metrics, Lines of Effort, breakthrough activities, and tracking implementation milestones. Assists the Executive Director and Deputy with program and project management, coordinating with subject matter experts, monitoring execution, and preparing status reports. Meets with internal customers and stakeholders to assess program performance, resolve issues, and communicate leadership intent. Gathers and analyzes program data, reviews integration and assessment reports, and briefs leadership on program status and outcomes. Develops and delivers tailored data products, including ad hoc extracts and recurring reports in multiple formats and media. Prepares business plans, documentation, fact sheets, point papers, and briefings, presenting recommendations and updates to management. Read the entire announcement before starting the application process. HR does not select or change your eligibility/eligibilities for you, regardless of the supporting documents you submit. You are considered ONLY for the eligibility or eligibilities you select and for which you provide all required supporting documents. You will not be considered if you do not select an eligibility. If you have questions about which eligibility/eligibilities apply to you, contact the HR POC listed on this announcement.

Details.JobSummary: Store Associates work either independently or as part of a team in any assigned retail area of a commissary store within the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) system, performing a variety of duties including handling, preparing, and stocking grocery and produce items, and checking-out customer purchases. Specific assignments vary by individual store and store management requirements.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: As an international grocery chain, the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) operates 235 commissaries throughout the world, with annual sales of more than $4 billion. We are proud to support military family readiness and enhance quality of life for our military service members and their families through this valued benefit. The foundation for our mission success is our people. We are more than 13,000 strong and reflect our nation's diverse cultures and backgrounds. We are a grocery store and a whole lot more. More information.
MajorDuties: Assisting customers by answering questions such as item price or location, and handling bulky/heavy items. Operating an electronic checkout system to record unit price, total customer purchase, and make change. Reviewing stock levels and gathering inventory data in order to maintain the Computer Assisted Ordering (CAO) system. Preparing and maintaining a variety of documents to order commissary items, reconcile invoices and submit requisitions. Maintaining security, safety, and sanitation practices and procedures. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is located at Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri. This is a Direct Hire Solicitation
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: As an integrated health care system, the Defense Health Agency delivers healthcare services across the Department of Defense and enables combat support to the Joint Force as a strategic partner. Through a robust healthcare delivery system, and a dedicated team of inspired professionals, the Agency ensures the worldwide delivery of medical, dental, and pharmacy programs to more than 9.5 million uniformed service members, retirees, and their families, by improving health and building readiness Anytime, Anywhere-Always.
MajorDuties: Evaluate and monitor medical service contracts.
Schedule and conduct contractor performance evaluations using a variety of methods.
Compare and evaluate the acceptability of the contractor based on the criteria outlined in the contract service summaries.
Notify senior leadership, contracting officer and functional commander of unacceptable contractor performance.
Initiate and submit contract discrepancy report or corrective action report to contractor for unacceptable performance.
Maintain a complete audit trail of all inspections and contract documentation.

Prepare, revise and maintain the Performance Work Statement, Statement of Work, QASP, independent government estimates, and other contract documents, ensuring the most current requirements are reflected.
Develop quality assurance criteria and contract surveillance processes using prior experience, knowledge, and terminology pertaining to service and maintenance contracts.
Research and identify appropriate labor rates, qualifications, materials and equipment, inflation, and applies appropriate data in preparing contract estimates and pricing/bidding schedules.
Prepare contract documents using a variety of computer program's and databases.
Coordinate a comprehensive plan to assure appropriate services are delivered in accordance with the contractual agreement.
Recommend changes in evaluation/sampling frequency, scope, or methodology.

Appointed as a multi-functional team member as a subject matter expert and participates in meetings with key personnel to discuss performance, procedures, review responses, and resolve problems and complaints.
Conduct on-site evaluations in support of identified short or long range service and requirements.

Details.Benefits: Working for Army Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF) can offer numerous advantages. Army NAF employment can provide a sense of pride and fulfillment, as you'll be supporting communities comprised of military and civilian personnel, and their families, which contributes to the Department of Defense's overall mission. Details.Benefits: Working for Army Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF) can offer numerous advantages. Army NAF employment can provide a sense of pride and fulfillment, as you'll be supporting communities comprised of military and civilian personnel, and their families, which contributes to the Department of Defense's overall mission. We offer a wide range of career opportunities, including jobs in childcare, recreation, hospitality, and more. Many employees have opportunities for professional development, including training, education, and certification programs to help towards career advancement. As an Army NAF employee, you'll have access to some on-base facilities, including fitness centers, libraries, and many other amenities. Regular full-time and part-time employees are eligible for enrollment in health and life insurance, participation in 401k and retirement plans, and paid personal time off and federal holidays. NAF flexible employees, working in the United States or a U.S. citizen or spouse or child of a U.S. citizen working for a NAFI in a foreign area, are eligible to participate in the NAF 401(k) plan. Some flexible employees may also be eligible to receive health insurance. For a slideshow presentation regarding these benefits, please click the Review Our Benefits link below.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the War Media Activity. The incumbent oversees the account management of all WEB.mil webhosting customers and the cost management for all WEB.mil business activities. Primary coordinator, reviewer, consultant, and accounts and costs manager for WEB.mil customer base of 1,000+ distinct, interoperable web sites. Conducts cost analyses and develops cost models to fund customer webhosting and any special projects.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: This position is located in the Web Enterprise Business (WEB.mil), Business Operations Office at the War Media Activity (WMA), Fort George G. Meade, Maryland, a Department of War Field Activity reporting to the Assistant to the Secretary of War (Public Affairs) (ATSW (PA)). WMA is a worldwide media organization charged with informing Department of War (DoW) audiences, managing the Department's visual information records, training the Department's public affairs and visual information workforce and providing broadcast radio and television to DoW personnel overseas operating from multiple locations in the United States and overseas, including deployed combat and contingency forces worldwide.
MajorDuties: As a PROGRAM ANALYST at the GS-0343-13 some of your typical work assignments may include: Master of rate and budget formulation, cost accounting, and customer-reimbursement transactions. Deep understanding of financial management and reporting. Maintain program financial stability which is a critical responsibility is ensuring the fund maintains a net positive cash balance to avoid Anti-Deficiency Act violations. Adjustments must be made to absorb annual gains or losses through future rate changes or, if necessary, by requesting additional appropriations from Congress. Mastery of regulatory compliance, including knowledge of the DoD Financial Management Regulation (FMR) 7000.14-R and relevant fiscal law is required to ensure compliance with the rules governing revolving funds.

Army CES positions apply Veteran's Preference to preference eligible candidates, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 3005, "CES Employment and Placement". If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. In order to qualify, you must meet the requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe one year specialized experience that demonstrates the possession of knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Such experience is typically in or directly related to the work of the position to be filled. Specialized experience would be demonstrated by 1) Directing collaborative strategic or operational planning with national, interagency or external partners to establish formal operational agreements and Standard Operating Procedures. 2) Conducting research to advise leadership on recommended operational Courses of Action and managing all facets of complex, multi-stakeholder or interagency planning meetings, from agenda-setting to action-item tracking. 3) Developing strategic guidance from internal teams, supporting the execution of operational or contingency plans, and leading post-event analysis or after-action reviews. 4) Providing analytical support for high-priority, short-suspense tasks, ensuring the coordinated and effective execution of leadership directives across diverse organizational stakeholders.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is a DOD Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system position in the Excepted Service under 10 USC 1599f. Employees occupying CES positions are in the Excepted Service and must adhere to U.S. Code, Title 10, as well as Department of Defense Instruction 1400.25. This position is located at the U.S. Cyber Command in Fort Meade, Maryland..
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Direct strategic planning and inter-agency collaboration with national partners (CNMF, USCYBERCOM) to forge critical information-sharing agreements and operational frameworks.
Advise senior leadership by delivering data-driven analysis and recommending Courses of Action (COAs) for complex cyberspace challenges.
Manage the full lifecycle of planning initiatives, ensuring strict security compliance while overseeing meeting logistics, documentation, and high-stakes action items.
Integrate national partner capabilities into active cyberspace operations by developing guidance, identifying opportunities, and refining contingency plans.
Drive continuous improvement by leading post-event analysis to translate lessons learned into enhanced strategies and operational processes.
Provide rapid, decisive analytical support on high visibility, time-sensitive cyberspace issues to enable effective leadership decisions.
Execute approved operational plans, facilitates coordinated action among diverse stakeholders, and provides analytical support for core business functions.

Develops and implements performance standards, makes or recommends selections for senior positions, and provides authoritative direction on policies and procedures.
Oversees the rigorous training, certification, and readiness of all subordinate JOC watch standers.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Secure the Domain. Defend the Nation. If you want to tackle complex cyber threats and directly support national security, the Department of War Cyber Defense Command (DCDC) is where you belong.We actively defend the War Department's global networks, ensuring the President and our Joint military forces maintain resilient command and control anywhere in the world. We offer our elite workforce cutting-edge technical training, rapid career growth, and exceptional quality-of-life programs. Step into the cyber domain and secure the mission. Visit https://www.dcdc.mil/ to learn more. This position is in the Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It is being recruited under 10 U.S.C. 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system. MajorDuties: Evaluates the progress of implementing master plans, objectives, and fund utilization, analyzing deviations and identifying the basis for delays, slippages, and overruns.
Develops and interprets policies, procedures, and methods for the administrative management and control of assigned programs, ensuring compliance with applicable laws and regulations.
Analyzes a wide range of programmatic data, including funding, contracts, and schedules, to identify potential problems and formulate corrective or improvement actions.
Coordinates with senior management and customers to formulate and review acquisition plans, milestones, schedules, and resource requirement determinations for various programs.
Develops and implements new program assessment techniques, metrics, and procedures to enable consistent program review and assessment across a diverse project portfolio.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Conduct comprehensive analyses to provide the supervisor, J3, and Command leadership with recommendations and to inform Commander decisions to allocate cyber forces to meet combatant command requirements.

Coordinate with Combatant Commanders/Services/Agencies to conduct these comprehensive assessments and make recommendations to the Commander and Secretary of Defense as to joint sourcing solutions for cyber forces.

Provide analytical expertise and operational insights to ensure these analyses realistically balance the operational risk of executing campaign plans, combat operations, crisis responses, and other assigned missions against available forces.

Build and maintain effective working relationships with colleagues throughout the DoD cyberspace community, as well as with external partners in the intelligence community, other U.S. Government (USG) agencies, and allied nations

Build and maintain a suite of analytical methodologies that is capable of capturing and accurately weighing the many factors that play into defining cyberspace force requirements to achieve national defense-critical operations
Coordinate and collaborate with and provides joint force allocation functional expertise and analytical skills to current operations activities,exercises, and assessments

Utilizing data models to make predictions Creating data visualizations to draw conclusions Synthesizing conclusions drawn from data analyses OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Business Administration OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Establish and govern the overarching data integration strategy and analytics policies for the J8 directorate, ensuring alignment with broader Department of War (DoW) and Joint Staff data stewardship mandates.

Direct the architecture and implementation of enterprise-scale Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) ecosystems utilizing advanced structured query languages and top-tier Microsoft enterprise data management solutions.
Define and enforce uncompromising data quality assurance and security protocols, guaranteeing the absolute integrity and authoritative nature of data used for command-level resource assessments

Serve as the lead technical authority in designing, building, and governing highly scalable, enterprise-wide data models that synthesize the most complex, unstructured Joint service datasets into cohesive strategic frameworks.

Pioneer advanced computational techniques and structural theories to build enterprise semantic layers and sophisticated forecasting models that anticipate global cyber resource gaps and capability requirements.

Direct the J8 portfolio of strategic decision-support tools, exclusively utilizing Microsoft Power BI and related Microsoft enterprise applications to build the command's most critical executive dashboards.
Distill massive, multi-domain datasets into highly intuitive, interactive formats tailored specifically for the Commander, USCYBERCOM, and Senior DoW Leadership.

Govern the integration of live, authoritative data feeds into enterprise Power BI workspaces, providing Command leadership with an undisputed, real-time operating picture of budget execution, acquisition pipelines, and global cyber readiness.

Serve as the definitive J8 technical representative, translating intricate analytical findings, advanced forecasting models, and complex data environments into definitive, actionable policy recommendations
Author overarching strategic analytical summaries, command-level technical architectures, and definitive executive read-aheads that shape DoW policy and influence congressional funding defense

Regularly deliver, aggressively defend, and contextualize high-stakes briefings to the highest levels of leadership, ensuring analytical confidence levels and strategic risks are implicitly understood by final decision-makers.

Details.JobSummary: Project Directors supply timely, accurate, and relevant information to assist senior leadership, customers, and/or management in making decisions. They contribute to the management of a project in technical, development, business, and operational functional organizations.
MajorDuties: Project Director responsibilities may include: - Developing and overseeing project plans as well as day-to-day activities. - Leading blended teams of contractors and civilians. - Understanding of or experience in managing Agile software development projects. - Performing requirements management, resource management and quality assurance oversight. - Developing and tracking schedules. - Monitoring performance goals and mitigating risks. - Leading/mentoring junior staff. - Creating and sustaining a strong customer focus with key stakeholders. - Collaborating with and building relationships with others to accomplish goals. - Presenting project status and informational briefs to senior leadership.
Details.Evaluations: The ideal candidate is someone who has previous project management experience with additional skills and experience in one or more of the following preferred: - Experience managing or overseeing hardware and/or software projects. - Certifications in DAWIA Program Management or PMP Certification. - Experience with fiscal, acquisition and/or contractual management processes. - Military experience and/or Department of Defense/Intelligence Community collaboration. - Knowledge of or experience with High Performance Computing (HPC) or Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure (HCI). - Knowledge of or experience with data warehousing, analytic hosting, streaming or real-time platforms. - Mission management. These ideal candidates will also have interest in continual learning and will possess strong communication (oral and written), problem-solving, analytic, interpersonal skills, and are: - results-oriented and accountable. - a critical thinker, able to take action in complex situations. - able to negotiate with and influence others. - able to manage multiple tasks with competing timelines and deliverables. - resourceful in identifying and consulting appropriate Subject Matter Experts to provide input on decisions. - competent in MS Office, including MS Project.
